A1.justification: Despite the retitling and SAIL-to-SILVR renaming, both PDFs describe the same evolving research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison. Changes in experimental conditions require care when comparing results, but do not prevent comparison of the documents.

before.justification: V1 reports original MetaWorld simulations and Panda-arm experiments, including success rates, filtering and initialization ablations, and rollout visualizations in Section 4 and Appendices C–E.

after.justification: V2 reports original simulation and real-robot results, including policy comparisons, distillation, component ablations and sequential-task demonstrations in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: V2's main MetaWorld implementation replaces v1's frozen MLP inverse-dynamics model with a diffusion inverse-dynamics model predicting action chunks, jointly fine-tuned with the video model. Internet-video adaptation becomes optional, VLM-based success filtering is introduced, and Algorithm 1 adds optional distillation into a diffusion policy. These are substantive procedural changes beyond renaming.

E1.justification: Although MetaWorld and Panda remain the environments, task coverage changes substantially. V2 adds faucet, handle, plate and wall-constrained manipulation tasks, while tasks such as Assembly, Lever Pull, Coffee Push and ordinary Button Press disappear. Appendix G.4 adds ordered multi-cup sequences beyond the retained individual cup-pushing and drawer-opening tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated BCIL comparisons in simulation and on real robots, and DSRL comparisons on MetaWorld, including suboptimal initialization results (Table 1, Figure 3 and Table A10). The prior-versus-no-prior comparison remains under SILVR terminology. V1's PA alternative in Table A6 and relabeling comparison in Figure 4 are removed.

E3.justification: The MetaWorld design changes from seven training tasks and six evaluated tasks, including one seen task, to eight training tasks and twelve unseen evaluation tasks. Reported video fine-tuning learning rate changes from 1e-5 to 1e-6. Evaluation extends from iterations 0–2 to 0–4 and additionally 0–9. New policy comparisons and distillation introduce their own training protocols, including 120 teacher-collected demonstrations.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of ten-iteration saturation, GPT-5/Gemini filtering, joint versus individual component updates, and DSRL update budgets (Figure 4, Figure 5, Tables A7 and A11). It substantially revises the suboptimal-initialization analysis and adds prior-effect comparisons and explicit failure cases in Appendix G. V1's PA and relabeling ablations are dropped.

E5.justification: Both versions already report MetaWorld results over three seeds; there is no documented increase in that count. V2 explicitly identifies the reported dispersion as standard deviation and includes uncertainty for aggregate averages in Tables 1, A8 and A9. V1's Tables A5–A6 provide per-task ± values but leave average rows without uncertainty.

E6.justification: V1's six-task SAIL results, averaging 24.4% to 34.4% across iterations 0–2, are replaced by differently configured twelve-task results reaching 44.2% at iteration 4 and 53.1% at iteration 9. V2 adds baseline, VLM-filtering, distillation and component-ablation results. These are not same-setting gains over v1. Existing real-robot prior/no-prior results are largely retained, with the two cup colors averaged in Figure 3.

T1.justification: The IPA score-composition equation remains unchanged. However, v1 Appendix D.1's explicit PA sampling formulation, Equation 2, and its mathematical contrast with IPA are removed. Neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V1 presents internet-video adaptation as critical to the improvement loop. V2 reframes the contribution around visual planning with optional internet priors and adds central claims of superior self-improvement and sample efficiency relative to behavior cloning and RL fine-tuning. Policy distillation for efficient deployment also becomes a claimed contribution.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the importance of internet priors by environment and reports a stronger dependence on filtering in its revised simulation setting. It adds hypotheses about visual-planning generalization, saturation and exploration, task-dependent benefits of suboptimal data, and why both planning components require updating. Appendix G.5 distinguishes semantic and execution failures. The basic limitation concerning insufficient initial success already existed in v1.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds substantial implementation information for the diffusion IDM, including latent inputs, temporal conditioning, action chunks and training schedules. It also documents BCIL, DSRL and policy-distillation budgets, batch sizes and learning rates. V2 adds a reproducibility statement; much of the existing video-model, hardware and real-robot implementation information is retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the video-customization discussion, including DreamBooth and DreamVideo, with positioning against diffusion-policy RL fine-tuning. New references include Diffusion Policy, ResIP, DPPO and DSRL. The research argument shifts substantially toward visual planning versus direct action policies and their online sample efficiency. ResIP and DPPO are discussed rather than experimentally evaluated.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and SAIL becomes SILVR. The abstract, introduction, contribution narrative and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Experiments are reorganized around filtered fine-tuning, internet priors, saturation/distillation, filtering signals and initialization quality. Appendices are reorganized and expanded, and a separate reproducibility section is introduced.

P2.justification: V2 revises the framework diagram, introduces a main comparison table, restructures the principal performance plots and combines the two cup-color panels. New saturation, distillation and initialization displays substantially change the visual presentation. Most earlier rollout montages are retained and relocated, alongside new comparative, sequential-task and failure-case figures. The document also adopts ICLR formatting.

improvement.justification: V1's principal comparisons were against variants of its own planner over iterations 0–2, leaving advantages over direct policy learning and longer-term behavior largely untested. V2 addresses these deficiencies with BCIL/DSRL comparisons, longer runs, component and update-budget ablations, and explicit failure analysis. Its more qualified discussion of internet priors also improves the account of applicability. Although earlier PA/relabeling analyses are removed and changed MetaWorld settings prevent direct version-to-version performance claims, the stronger validation and implementation documentation constitute a substantial overall improvement.
